c: The Copper Spoon, a 90-seat full-service restaurant
s: The Copper Spoon's food cost has risen to 38% of sales. Servers say dishes often run out during dinner, while the walk-in cooler contains spoiled produce and unlabeled containers.
The owner (judge) wants you to explain how to control food costs, organize storage and ordering, and make sure food is safe.
p: Maintain inventory of supplies
Place orders/reorders
Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs
Describe health and safety regulations in business
Identify quality-control measures
n: Uses par levels, regular counts and a first-in, first-out system
Orders based on forecasts and sales history
Tracks waste, portion sizes and menu item costs
Labels and dates food, monitors temperatures and keeps records
Samples and inspects deliveries for quality
q: A supplier delivers fish that smells off. What do you do?
How would you reduce food cost without lowering quality?

c: Bella Notte, an Italian restaurant known for date nights
s: Bella Notte's reservations are strong but reviews mention long waits after guests are seated, orders that are forgotten, and a server who ignored a guest's anniversary request.
The general manager (judge) wants you to explain how to provide excellent dining service, how to recover from mistakes, and how to coach servers.
p: Build and maintain relationships with customers
Handle customer/client complaints
Demonstrate a customer service mindset
Respond to customer inquiries
Recognize/Reward others for their efforts and contributions
n: Greets guests, notes occasions and checks back at the right moments
Apologizes, replaces the dish and may comp an item or dessert
Staff anticipate needs and take ownership
Answers menu and allergy questions accurately
Recognizes servers who deliver outstanding service
q: A guest says their steak is overcooked after eating half of it. What do you do?
How do you handle two servers who both claim a table?

s: Smoke & Ember BBQ has lost six servers and two cooks in the past two months. The owner wants to understand why, and hire people who stay.
The owner (judge) wants you to explain how to recruit, onboard and keep restaurant employees, and how to treat staff fairly.
p: Discuss the nature of human resources management
Orient new employees
Explain the role of ethics in human resources management
Motivate team members
Solicit feedback
n: Describes recruiting, hiring, training and retaining
Uses a checklist, shadowing and a buddy during the first week
Fair scheduling, equal treatment and compliance with wage laws
Recognition, growth paths and clear communication
Conducts surveys and stay interviews
q: A server says they are leaving because of schedule changes at the last minute. What do you do?
How do you make sure new hires do not feel lost?

c: Harbor Grill, a waterfront seafood restaurant
s: Harbor Grill is quiet on Monday and Tuesday nights. The manager wants to build weeknight traffic through a regular event, such as live music or a chef's tasting night.
The general manager (judge) wants you to explain how to plan the event, how to promote it to locals and tourists, and how to measure results.
d: present your event and promotion plan
p: Plan special events
Explain communications channels used in public-relations activities
Describe word-of-mouth channels used to communicate with targeted audiences
Develop promotional calendar
Identify ways to track marketing-communications activities
n: Sets goals, costs, menu and staffing for the event
Partners with local media and community groups
Encourages guests to share photos and invite friends
Schedules promotion before, during and after the event
Tracks reservations, sales, coupon use and social engagement
q: How would you decide whether to keep the weeknight event after two months?
What would you do if the event brought a large crowd and the kitchen could not keep up?

s: Olive & Thyme Bistro is busy, but the owner is not sure the restaurant is making a profit. Cash is tight at the end of each month, and the owner has never reviewed an income statement.
The owner (judge) wants you to explain what financial reports a restaurant should review, what key costs to watch and how to improve profit.
p: Describe the nature of income statements
Describe the nature of budgets
Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs
Identify factors affecting a business's profit
Describe the nature of cash flow statements
n: Income statement shows sales, cost of goods sold, labor, rent and profit
Compares results to a budget and finds variances
Overhead includes rent, utilities and insurance
Profit is affected by pricing, waste, labor, theft and volume
Cash flow shows timing of money in and out
q: Which cost would you review first if profits fell 5% in a month?
Why can a busy restaurant still run out of cash?
